title: Cap. IX: Garissoles (3) — softens decimandi impropriety; Heb. 7:5–6 already uses it bare
pass_a_gloss: After that useless skirmish Garissoles's third point: we take the more common reading, ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν as 'so to speak,' and those words fit softening the Apostle's statement. Placeus: that does not wound our cause. The softener, if any, targets the verb of tithing, not the doctrinal matter. Properly one tithes goods, not persons, when a tenth is taken out. So the oddity of saying 'Levi was tithed' (meaning tithes were taken from Levi) is what Garissoles thinks Paul meant to ease with ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν. Placeus marvels that a learned man missed the page: Paul already used the same verb twice without any softener — Hebrews 7:5 ἀποδεκατοῦν τὸν λαόν ('they tithe the people') and 7:6 δεδεκάτωκεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ ('he tithed Abraham'). So Paul was not softening that use of the tithing verb.
pass_b_english: After this useless skirmish he adds, third: "Yet we do this and follow the more common position — ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, 'so to speak.' The words are therefore fitted for softening the Apostle's saying." This does our cause no harm at all. For that reason for softening is to be referred not to the matter itself, but rather to the verb of tithing. Persons are not properly tithed, but goods — as everyone knows — when a tenth part is taken out of them. So because there is a certain impropriety in saying that Levi was tithed, for what is meant — that tithes were taken from Levi — therefore, he thinks, the Apostle judged this oddity should be softened by the little words ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν. I marvel that this slipped from a learned man. He does not seem to have looked at the place. For he would have seen the Apostle already twice use that same verb in the same way without any softening: once in verse 5 — ἀποδεκατοῦν τὸν λαόν, "they tithe the people" — and again in verse 6 — δεδεκάτωκεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, "he tithed Abraham." Therefore the Apostle did not mean to soften the verb of tithing when used that way.
source_text: Praemissa hac inutili velitatione, subjungit, 3. Nos tamen facimus ac positionem communiorem sequimur, ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, ut ita dicam. Verba sunt ergo molliendo dicto Apostoli apposita. Hoc quidem causae nostrae nihil praejudicat. Illa enim molliendi ratio, non rem ipsam, sed potius ad verbum decimandi referenda est. Non enim personae, proprie decimantur, sed bona, ut notum est, cum ex eis decima pars excerpitur. Ergo quia quaedam improprietas est in eo quod Levi decimatus dicitur, pro eo quod est, decimas ex Levi acceptas fuisse, ideo existimavit Apostolus hanc ἀτοπίαν esse leniendam per voculas, ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν. Miror hoc excidisse Viro docto. Non videtur inspexisse locum. Vidisset enim Apostolum jam bis absque ulla emollitione verbum illud eodem modo usurpasse, semel vers. 5. ἀποδεκατοῦν τὸν λαόν dicens, decimant populum & iterum vers. 6. δεδεκάτωκεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, decimavit Abrahamum. Non igitur decimandi verbum sic usurpatum emollire voluit Apostolus.
